Indian equity benchmarks extended their winning streak to a fifth consecutive session on November 4, supported by a sustained decline in crude oil prices, renewed foreign fund inflows and strong domestic earnings. However, weak global cues and uncertainty surrounding the US midterm election outcome kept investors cautious.
At close, the Sensex was up 383.55 points or 0.50 percent at 77,301.40, and the Nifty was up 149.75 points or 0.63 percent at 23,960.60.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Gains)
GIFT Nifty was trading firm at around 24,313.50 in early trade, indicating a strong start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Mixed)
Asian stocks were mixed as consumer and financial stocks rose following gains in US equities, while investors rotated away from semiconductor shares.

The majority of stocks in the MSCI Asia Pacific Index gained after the S&P 500 Index jumped 1.6% on Wednesday, its biggest advance in three months, and the Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.9%. South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi Index dropped 3.6%, reflecting investor concerns over the future of data-center development and losses in US chip stocks.
US Equities (Gain)

Wall Street closed sharply higher on Wednesday as Democrats' sweeping midterm election victory eased political uncertainty and boosted risk appetite, though ​data center shares fell on fears of tighter AI regulation.

The S&P 500 gained ⁠119.7 points, or 1.6%, to end at 7,688.62 points, while the Nasdaq Composite added 364.50 points, or 1.4%, to 25,736.51. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,569.40 points, or 3%, to 53,356.12.
Dollar Index (Slips)
The dollar edged lower on Thursday in the aftermath of an overwhelming victory by Democrats in US midterm elections that cleared a major source of uncertainty and fuelled a rally in global equities.
US Bond Yield (Down)
Treasury yields fell across the curve on Wednesday as the Democrats won control of both chambers of the Congress.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury fell 2 basis points at 4.86%, while 2-year bond down nearly 2 basis points at 4.56%.
Asian Currencies (Up)

Asian currencies traded mostly higher against the US dollar, with the Philippine peso emerging as the top gainer, rising 0.36 percent, followed by the Thai baht, which strengthened 0.42 percent. The Japanese yen and Malaysian ringgit appreciated 0.29 percent each, while the South Korean won and Singapore dollar gained 0.18 percent and 0.08 percent, respectively.
On the other hand, the Taiwan dollar weakened 0.21 percent, while the Chinese renminbi and Indonesian rupiah declined 0.07 percent and 0.04 percent, respectively, against the US dollar.
Crude (Down)
Brent oil steadied after tumbling more than 8% in the previous session as investors bet that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could accelerate efforts to end the war in the Middle East.
Gold (Up)
Gold held the biggest surge since August after a Democratic sweep of Congress in US midterm elections sent the dollar and Treasury yields lower, boosting its appeal.
Bullion was trading around $4,070 an ounce, after jumping 3.3% the previous session.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) extended their buying streak to a fourth consecutive session, purchasing equities worth Rs 7,284 crore on November 4. In contrast, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued their selling for the fourth straight session, offloading equities worth Rs 3,712 crore.
